## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyabhikkhādāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 28), translated as the *Second Alms Giver’s Mansion*, is a canonical verse text in the *Vimānavatthu* collection. The narrative centers on the karmic efficacy of generosity, illustrating how offering alms with a joyful, pure, and tranquil mind yields bountiful celestial rewards. The text has been translated into at least five modern languages.

Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive formulaic connections within Pali literature, identifying 179 matching passages shared across 24 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. In addition to extensive overlap with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the text shares nearly its entire sequence (§0.1–7.1) with its immediate counterpart, the *Paṭhamabhikkhādāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 27), and exhibits substantial shared verse segments with other mansion accounts, such as the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dutiyasūcivimānavatthu* (Vv 59), *Dutiyasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 14), and *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records weak computational alignments with a Tibetan text (BO_K01_D0007B-2_H0008-2), though these represent machine text-reuse matches rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
